item.title: Trump Fired His Inspectors General. Their Replacements Have a Different Mission.
item.description: President Trump is installing his allies in the offices of inspector general, which are meant to provide independent government oversight.
item.dc:creator: Luke Broadwater
item.media:credit: Al Drago for The New York Times
item.media:description: President Trump has inserted a conservative operative to take over the inspector general’s office in charge of any internal investigation into his botched repairs of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.

item.title: Judge Allows Limited Testing in Trump Plan to Paint Eisenhower Building White
item.description: A federal judge ruled that initial preparatory steps, including testing out paints on the building’s gray granite exterior, could proceed for now.
item.dc:creator: Zach Montague
item.media:credit: Allison Robbert for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Eisenhower Executive Office Building in May.

item.title: A Missile Alert Half a World Away Interrupts Court Hearing at Guantánamo
item.description: A possible expert witness was hurried off a video feed after an emergency alert in Dubai, near the Strait of Hormuz, a flashpoint in the U.S.-Iran war.
item.dc:creator: Carol Rosenberg
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Marisa Schwartz Taylor/The New York Times
item.media:description: Prosecutors previewing testimony in a pretrial hearing at the war court in Guantánamo Bay, Cuba, were interrupted by a missile alert in Dubai.

item.title: Minnesota Sues Texas Gov. Greg Abbott Over His Refusal to Extradite ICE Agent
item.description: A federal agent facing assault charges in Minnesota has been jailed in Texas since May. Gov. Greg Abbott has not granted an extradition request.
item.dc:creator: Ernesto Londoño
item.media:credit: Christopher Lee for The New York Times
item.media:description: Gov. Greg Abbott of Texas at an event in Kerrville in July.

item.title: Florida’s Polling Picture Is Limited Other Than One Key Race
item.description: Representative Byron Donalds had a wide lead in polls of the race for the Republican nomination for governor. Polling was sparse in every other statewide contest.
item.dc:creator: Evan Reynolds
item.media:credit: Zack Wittman for The New York Times
item.media:description: Florida is holding primaries for a Senate seat, the governor’s office and several competitive House races.

item.title: Hurricane Lala Destroyed a Hawaii Cemetery, Setting Off a Hunt for the Dead
item.description: In the hamlet of Naalehu, the floods of Hurricane Lala opened graves. One mother sought desperately for her son.
item.dc:creator: Meghan Miner Murray
item.media:credit: Meghan Miner Murray
item.media:description: The storm turned the small cemetery into torrents of mud, bearing the detritus of death.

item.title: Here’s the latest.
item.description: Voters in Alaska, Wyoming and Florida are nominating candidates for governor and the U.S. Senate on Tuesday, and a California district will move one step closer to finding a replacement for its disgraced former Congressman.
item.dc:creator: Bayliss Wagner

item.title: Google Just Made It Easier for Campaigns to Send You Fund-Raising Emails
item.description: Republicans previously sued Google claiming its spam filter was biased, but the case was dismissed. The company will now allow verified campaigns to more easily bypass the spam filter.
item.dc:creator: Shane Goldmacher
item.media:credit: Kelsey McClellan for The New York Times
item.media:description: Google has updated Gmail’s policy to allow political committees to more easily bypass its spam filter when sending emails for donations, allowing more political ads to land in inboxes.

item.title: An A.I. Tax Boom Could Curtail America’s Debt. But Not Solve It.
item.description: The consequences of A.I. for the budget will largely hinge on whether — and to what extent — the technology reshapes the labor market.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Duehren
item.media:credit: Nick Little

item.title: 2 Workers Die After Explosions and Fire at Ohio Recycling Plant
item.description: Chemical tanks had ruptured during the incident but officials said there was no immediate threat to the Toledo area.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Wolfe and Johnny Diaz
item.media:credit: WTVG, via Associated Press
item.media:description: This image, taken from video provided by WTVG, shows firefighters working on the scene after an explosion at an industrial recycling business in Toledo, Ohio, on Tuesday.

item.title: Trump Takes Aim at CNN Reporter Kristen Holmes During Event to Honor California Lifeguard
item.description: President Trump told a journalist to “be quiet” at a White House event for a California lifeguard and a boy he saved.
item.dc:creator: Ali Watkins
item.media:credit: Doug Mills/The New York Times
item.media:description: President Trump met with lifeguard Ryder Williams, left, and Nathaniel Rai, right, in the Oval Office on Monday.

item.title: Residents on Hawaii’s Big Island Look to Help One Another After Hurricane Lala
item.description: In a remote region of the ravaged Big Island, there were community gas runs, donated turkey stuffing, a makeshift emergency broadcast and even a helicopter.
item.dc:creator: Orlando Mayorquín
item.media:credit: Ronit Fahl for The New York Times
item.media:description: Brandy Field, from Ka’u Radio, helps to set up internet access in Ocean View, Hawaii, on Monday after Hurricane Lala. The storm knocked out power to thousands on the Big Island.

item.title: In Los Angeles, the San Fernando Valley Celebrates Itself on 818 Day
item.description: The Valley is often ignored in Los Angeles discussions, and residents once tried to secede from the city. But on one day each year, the region gets its recognition.
item.dc:creator: Tim Arango and Shawn Hubler
item.media:credit: Ariana Drehsler for The New York Times
item.media:description: Separated by the Santa Monica Mountains from downtown, Dodger Stadium and Hollywood, the Valley rarely gets the spotlight.

item.title: Florida Primary Underscores State’s New Identity as a Republican Juggernaut
item.description: Republicans hold every statewide elected office and have drastically swung voter registration in the state. A newly gerrymandered congressional map has added four Republican-leaning seats.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei
item.media:credit: Paul Hennessy/Anadolu, via Getty Images
item.media:description: So few potentially competitive districts remain in Florida that a majority of the state’s 28 congressional races will be all but settled in the primaries.

item.title: Searching for Answers From the Man Accused of Sabotaging Alaska’s Senate Race
item.description: Dan Sullivan, a retired schoolteacher from tiny Petersburg, Alaska, shares a name with the incumbent senator he hopes to defeat. Is he a spoiler trying to divide the Republican vote? We traveled to Alaska to find out.
item.dc:creator: Kellen Browning and Christopher Miller

item.title: What to Watch in Tuesday’s Primary Elections in Alaska, Florida and Beyond
item.description: An early glimpse of a pivotal Senate race, heated primaries on a newly redrawn congressional map, and a special election to replace Eric Swalwell will be in the spotlight on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk
item.media:credit: Associated Press
item.media:description: Senator Dan S. Sullivan and former Representative Mary Peltola are both widely expected to advance in Alaska’s Senate primary, but their vote shares will be closely watched as a reflection of who’s ahead going into the general election.

item.title: Texas Tech University Is Using A.I. to Cut Left-Leaning Content
item.description: Texas Tech is using A.I. to cut left-leaning content in its curriculum. Some say the effort to ferret out forbidden topics is a dystopian academic nightmare.
item.dc:creator: Vimal Patel
item.media:credit: David Kozlowski/Getty Images
item.media:description: The Texas Tech campus in Lubbock is in a right-leaning part of the state. Its leader is trying to clamp down on teaching about gender and sexuality.

item.title: Judge Releases Woman Accused of Vandalizing World War II Memorial
item.description: Prosecutors led by Jeanine Pirro, the U.S. attorney in Washington, argued that Melissa Farris posed a flight risk and asked the court to reverse its decision.
item.dc:creator: Dan Watson
item.media:credit: Kylie Cooper/Reuters
item.media:description: National Guard troops patrolling the World War II Memorial in Washington after it was vandalized last week.

item.title: A California County Eyes a New Hire: Tina Peters, the Election Denier
item.description: The top elections official in Shasta County offered a job to Ms. Peters, a Trump supporter who was convicted of tampering with voting machines in Colorado.
item.dc:creator: Jack Healy

item.title: U.S. Airman Says He Would Accept Punishment for Protesting Iran War
item.description: Major Watson characterized the war in Iran as an act of American aggression and compared the U.S. military actions to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

item.title: Family Presses for Information About Fatal ICE Shooting in Maine
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security said there would be an investigation. But so far little has been disclosed about the killing last month.
item.dc:creator: Maia Spoto and Murray Carpenter
item.media:credit: Christopher Capozziello for The New York Times
item.media:description: Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, a Colombian immigrant, was killed by a federal agent on July 13 in Biddeford, Maine.

item.title: House Panel Investigates Charges a Democrat Had Sexual Contact With Aide
item.description: Representative Jimmy Gomez of California acknowledged “personal mistakes” outside his marriage but denied breaking rules that bar relationships with a direct subordinate.
item.dc:creator: Michael Gold
item.media:credit: Ian Maule for The New York Times
item.media:description: Mr. Gomez said that he regretted his mistakes, but he denied wrongdoing, saying that his actions “were consensual in nature and haven’t violated the law or House Ethics rules.”

item.title: Trump Votes by Mail Again in Florida
item.description: The president also voted by mail in 2020 and in a Florida special election in March, even as he has railed against the practice and equated it to cheating.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron
item.media:credit: Al Drago for The New York Times
item.media:description: President Trump has voted by mail in Palm Beach County at least twice before: Once in 2020 and earlier this year in a special election.

item.title: Judge Rules Trump Administration Can’t Scrap F.B.I. Move to Maryland
item.description: The ruling is almost certainly not the end of the lengthy fight over the F.B.I.’s future headquarters, which has lasted for years.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron

item.media:description: The J. Edgar Hoover F.B.I. Building in Washington last year. An imposing symbol of the F.B.I.’s vast federal powers when it opened in 1974, the building has long been deteriorating.

item.title: Appeals Court Rejects Trump’s Strategy of Picking U.S. Attorneys
item.description: It was the second federal appellate decision to take issue with the administration’s custom of leaving interim prosecutors in place to lead U.S. attorney’s offices to circumvent congressional approval.

item.title: Trump to Travel to Myrtle Beach to Rally for Darline Graham
item.description: The sister of Lindsey Graham was appointed to his Senate seat on an interim basis. She must win a runoff next week against a conservative House member to serve a full six-year term.
item.dc:creator: Emily Davies
item.media:credit: Doug Mills/The New York Times
item.media:description: President Trump is trying to consolidate support for Darline Graham, the sister of Senator Lindsey Graham, who died unexpectedly in July. Ms. Graham faces Representative Ralph Norman in a runoff election next week.
